transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
As Democrats prepare to take control of both chambers of Congress next year, there's competition
to be the new leaders.
Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen is challenging Chuck Schumer, who recruited the candidates
who ran and won in red states for Senate Majority Leader.
And Hakeem Jeffries is running for Speaker of the House.
And here's Mara Eliasson has more on their chances.
Well, there are Democrats who feel neither Jeffries nor Schumer fought as hard as they
should have against Trump for the last two years.
But it's hard to imagine that Jeffries won't be elected Speaker.
He just presided over the most dramatic victory Democratic House members have had in a generation.
Even if some progressives in the House caucus want someone else, he has a very big majority.
And the majority makers were those blue dogs and centrist Democrats that flipped red state
seats.
They made the majority in the House, not the liberals.
And here's Mara Eliasson.
Israel says it killed a top Hamas commander in southern Gaza.
And Hamas confirmed that, calling it a, quote, "cowardly assassination."
And here's Lauren Freire has more from Tel Aviv.
The Israeli military released grainy black and white aerial footage of a man walking alone
on a street lined with what looked like tents, then an explosion and debris.
It identified the target as Samir Mahmoud Hassan Abu Yunis.
Hamas confirms he was one of its senior commanders, a member of the organization's military wing
since 1991.
Hamas says he helped plan and supervise the October 7th attacks and pledged that his,
quote, "blood shall not be in vain."
Since those 2023 attacks and the Israeli assault on Gaza that followed, health officials say
Israeli attacks have killed more than 74,000 people in Gaza.
Lauren Freire, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
An online petition to bring Jensen Huang, back as CEO of the chipmaker NVIDIA, has more
than 160,000 names on it.
Huang resigned from the company last week following reports he had multiple extramarital
affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
And here's John Ruich has more.
The petition calls for Huang to be reinstated while the company conducts an independent
investigation.
It calls for details of the inquiry's scope, independence, and timeline, and asks for Huang
to be given an opportunity to respond before a final decision.
It says Huang deserves fairness.
According to statistics on the website where the "Stand with Jensen" petition is posted,
nearly 8,000 current NVIDIA employees have added their names to the letter.
That's out of more than 42,000 in total.
Tens of thousands of shareholders have also signed on.
Among the names are some well-known figures, including SpaceX and Tesla boss Elon Musk,
Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Zhang Yiming, the co-founder of TikTok's parent company
ByteDance.
John Ruich, NPR News.
This is NPR News.
Ukrainian President Zelensky says restrictions on his country's star-shield satellite system
are hindering its ability to intercept Russian drones.
And he's warning that the limitations imposed by Elon Musk's SpaceX could weaken defenses
around Ukraine's energy infrastructure as winter approaches.
Today, a Russian strike on corona-Morsk injured several people in damaged energy infrastructure,
leaving about 41,000 customers without power.
Meanwhile, Ukrainian drones damaged two electrical substations in Russia's Rostov region, killing
a chief engineer.
Andy Warhol's 1986 self-portrait goes up for auction Tuesday, and people can bet on
whether it will sell for more than $16 million.
It's part of a new partnership between the art market website ArtNet and the prediction
market, Kelshi.
And Piazzanastasia Tsiolkis has more.
ArtNet started out in 1989 as an online database to provide info on art auction sales.
Last year, it was acquired by venture capital firm Beowulf Capital.
Now ArtNet says it will help Kelshi curate the markets that users can bet on.
Critics of the deal say that art auctions already take place in a high-stakes, insular
world and that the chances of market manipulation are steep.
Some are also saying it's going to make the art world even more focused on money, not
creative expression.
The partnership was announced soon before the annual wintertime art fairs like Miami
Art Week commence.
Anastasia Tsiolkis, NPR News.

topics.text: Democrats weigh leadership contest as Chris Van Hollen challenges Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries runs for Speaker
Israel says it killed senior Hamas commander Samir Mahmoud Hassan Abu Yunis in southern Gaza
Online petition seeks reinstatement of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned over reported extramarital affairs
Zelensky says SpaceX restrictions on Starshield hinder Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian drones
Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia-area energy infrastructure leaves about 41,000 customers without power
Ukrainian drones damage two electrical substations in Russia's Rostov region, killing a chief engineer
Andy Warhol 1986 self-portrait heads to auction, with bets offered on sale price via Kalshi partnership with ArtNet
